Degener’s primary glossary explicitly analyzes sam well as probably from sāma, referring to Turner 13346 and attributing the suggestion to Buddruss. The full Turner entry groups sāmaka even/level and sāma likeness/sameness; it does not itself cite Shina. This is therefore a tentative semantic development from even/equal to well/good, supported by Degener’s qualified proposal rather than a direct Turner attestation. The head record represents that grouped entry; no unexplained -ka reflex is asserted. The Backstrom/Schmidt good attestations and the well attestation share sam, but their grammatical gloss differences are preserved.

CDIAL 10511 yuṣmad explicitly records Shina Gilgit tšo, Kohistani/Gurezi tso and Palesi co(h) in the second-person plural series. It explains the t-initial branch through influence from tuvam and the plural ending, rather than direct unchanged continuation of yuṣmad. These affricate forms match that cited dialect range; their generic you glosses and source-specific aspiration notation are retained without silently adding a modern number restriction. The sū/so and th- forms, and forms with extra endings, remain outside this group.

The survey’s satdezī/saddezī family denotes a week as seven days. Degener independently records sat seven and dees day with oblique plural deezo; CDIAL 13139 gives Shina sat/satt seven and 6333 explicitly gives Gilgit dez plural dēzi and Kohistani/Gurezi dēs plural dīzi. The two lexical components therefore account for the numeral plus plural noun. Preserve td versus assimilated dd, vowel length and the Darel ś spelling; these phonetic differences make the grouped dialect comparison qualified rather than an assertion of identical pronunciation.
